neighbours.label: unclear, weak pole (max 8.5): quantifier or verb introducing a described condition in academic prose about children's developmental or behavioural disorders ('with two types of ...', 'also experience ...')
fire: The trial enrolled preschoolers with two types of speech delay.
Researchers followed adolescents with two forms of attention disorder.
The survey included toddlers with two kinds of language impairment.
Interestingly, typically developing infants also experience similar sleep problems.
The paper describes pupils with two subtypes of developmental dyslexia.
Clinicians assessed boys with two patterns of impulsive behaviour.
The cohort comprised children with two categories of motor disorder.
Notably, healthy siblings also experience comparable mood swings.
quiet: The bakery sold pastries with two types of fruit filling.
Tourists followed the guide past two rows of market stalls.
The menu included sandwiches with two kinds of cheese.
Interestingly, the old harbour also has a small lighthouse.
The brochure describes cabins with two styles of wooden porch.
Gardeners planted beds with two shades of purple tulips.
The parade comprised floats with two bands of drummers.
Notably, the red bicycle also has a wicker basket.

notes: Card top examples have no shared token (implement, experience, two, taking, face, practice). Probe: only 'compared children with two types of reading difficulty' reached 0.22; the other card-like verbs 0.04-0.08. Recorded as a best guess that will probably fail.
